newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sage plans $40-50 mln foreign share issue.
newsitem.headline: Sage plans $40-50 mln foreign share issue.

text.p: South African insurer Sage Group Ltd said on Thursday it was planning an issue of $40-50 million of cumulative convertible redeemable preference shares for cash to offshore investors in Europe.
The planned issue, through Nomura International, will help the company pursue the expansion of its recent U.S. acquisition, Fidelity Standard Life Insurance Co, Sage said in a statement.

The issue, to be listed in Luxembourg, would be made up of 4,000 to 5,000 newly constituted preference shares, maturing 2001 and offering a dividend yield of 4.5 percent per annum, at a price of $10,000 each, Sage said.
The preference shares would be convertible into Sage ordinary shares at the holder's option and, two years after issue, would be redeemable at par at Sage's option under certain conditions.
Sage said redemption of unconverted preference shares at maturity would be at a premium based on the four-year U.S. T-bond rate at the time the issue was priced.
The issue was subject to shareholder approval, it said.
